name: Lonavala
shortIntro: The first ghat out of both cities, and the one everyone learns to ride on.
description: Lonavala sits on the Sahyadri crest between Mumbai and Pune, which is why it has been the default weekend escape for both for fifty years. For a rider it is the shortest distance between a city and a real climb: the old Khandala descent, the Tiger's Leap spur, and the quieter roads out towards Pawna that most traffic never finds.
rideNote: Ninety minutes from Pune, two and a half hours from Mumbai on the expressway — but ride the old NH-48 through Khandala instead. The expressway is faster and duller, and two-wheelers are not permitted on it.
roadNote: Good tarmac, heavy weekend traffic until you turn off towards Pawna or Aamby. Fog from June to September can drop visibility to a few metres by late afternoon.
bestSeason: October to February for clear roads; June to September if you want the green and will accept the fog.

name: Karjat
shortIntro: Rivers, base villages and the approach roads to half the Sahyadri treks.
description: Karjat is the flat land at the bottom of the ghats — farm country cut by the Ulhas river, with the wall of the Sahyadris standing over it. It is where riders stop before or after the climb, and where most of the region's farmhouse stays are.
rideNote: Roughly two hours from Mumbai via Panvel and Chowk. The Karjat–Khopoli stretch is one of the better short rides in the region.
roadNote: Mixed surface. The main roads are fine; the village roads towards the trek bases are narrow, unlit and shared with tractors.
bestSeason: July to September for the rivers, November to February for everything else.

name: Alibaug
shortIntro: Coast road, low sun, and a ferry that lets you skip the highway entirely.
description: Alibaug is the Konkan coast at its most reachable — a run of beaches from Kihim down to Kashid, with fishing villages, sea forts and coconut plantations between them. The riding is flat and fast, and the light in the last hour before sunset is the reason people keep coming back.
rideNote: Either the RoRo ferry from Bhaucha Dhakka with the bike on board, or the full road route around the creek through Panvel and Pen.
roadNote: Flat, generally good coastal tarmac. Sand drifts across the road near the beaches — brake early.
bestSeason: November to February. Avoid the peak of the monsoon unless you enjoy salt and rain together.

name: Pune
shortIntro: Not a destination so much as the doorway to every good road in the west.
description: Pune is where a great many rides start. Within two hours of the city you can be on the Tamhini ghat, at Lavasa, on the Sinhagad climb or heading south towards Panshet. Stays here are for the night before and the night after.
rideNote: The city itself is dense; plan an early exit. Tamhini, Mulshi and Sinhagad are all inside a two-hour window.
roadNote: Urban traffic, then good state highways once you clear the ring road.
bestSeason: Year-round as a base. The ghats around it are best from October to March.

name: Mumbai
shortIntro: Where most rides begin at four in the morning to beat the toll queue.
description: Mumbai is a starting line. Stays listed here are chosen for the things that matter the night before a ride — secure parking, a gate that opens early, and a location that puts you on the highway without crossing the city.
rideNote: Leave before 5am on a weekend or lose an hour at Panvel. The Eastern Freeway and Sion–Panvel are the usual exits south and east.
roadNote: City riding throughout. Potholes return with the monsoon and stay until November.

name: Goa
shortIntro: The long one. Eight hundred kilometres of coast road if you do it properly.
description: Goa is the ride south — either fast down NH-48 through Belgaum, or slow along the Konkan coast road with a hundred river crossings. What you find at the end is a different kind of stay: older houses, longer evenings, and roads that reward going nowhere in particular.
rideNote: Two days from Mumbai if you take the coast road, which is the only way worth taking. Bridges at Jaigad and Dabhol need ferry timings checked in advance.
roadNote: NH-66 is largely good with long construction stretches. The interior village roads are narrow and unmarked.
bestSeason: November to February. May is unbearable, June to September is beautiful and wet.
